title: a month into building North Atlantic islands in Unity with Claude Code
author: imlo2
selftext:
I've continued to work on this realtime environment generation system prototype for a month now.

This is the first island I generated instead of taking the form from real terrain heightmap.

The first videos I've shared showed an island shaped and modified from Lofoten elevation data. 

For this one I blocked out the big forms and the pipeline did the rest: relief, ravines, erosion, valleys carved where the water drains, lakes, the coast and the waves that reach it. The close-up fine ground detail stamps are currently borrowed from the real island's scan, so the rock still reads as rock, etc. Later this will be replaced with a procedural system or a learned model. Then the plants, trees and rocks are placed by the same rules as on the first island, none by hand, there's zero manual corrections after the generation so I left wonky stuff there, if there's any. 

So this was in essence the first proper test run of the island builder pipeline, and I think it was quite successful. 

The core idea is that the system can generate a few hundred square kilometres of terrain to be explored on foot, and it takes only a few minutes to set up something like this.

New environment system features since the last video:

* Trees: spruce, aspen, grey alder, rowan and juniper join the pines and birches, about 42,000 trees on this island.
* Ground: lingonberry, cotton grass in the bogs, and generally plant details have improved with more detailed leaves with normal, translucency etc. maps.
* A lot of more or less subtle improvements to the terrain detailing system, which fixes edge case issues in areas like some terrain type collisions, areas where transitions matter more than usually (like waterline, etc.)
* A selection of debug tooling for visuals have been added, which helps fixing more subtle geometry and shading errors (normals, various lighting components, albedo, light transmission, surface type, etc.) and can be enabled on the fly while the game runs or in edit mode.
* Night: the stars rebuilt, I'll replace them later with a real night sky star system.

How it's made: 

I direct and judge, look into issues, Claude Code builds it and fixes bugs. I set the look, pick the references, review every change by eye. Claude writes the code, shaders and tools, and measures its own work before I look. 

Claude made a small scale video editor for this project, and I've been using it, framed and cut the shots for this video (71 candidate views down to 36) and also the previous ones. And then a finalization was done automatically, so that cuts land exactly on the the music's beat, read from the track's MIDI. 

It runs well above 60 fps at 1440p on an RTX 3090. There's no sound yet.

I've still not decided what to make out of this - does it stay as a proof of concept, or will I develop a game out of it.  
  
Terrain detail based on Nasjonal høydemodell DTM 1 m, © Kartverket (CC BY 4.0), modified.

comments.author: Pulkownik
comments.body: How did you achieve this water? Did you prompt something specific?

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body:
Well there is nothing really specific; you can look from the literature what techniques are used for water effects nowadays in realtime graphics, and then ask Claude or Codex to build it. But I didn't prompt something like "create fancy water", instead I gave a few parameters and constraints what to try to implement first, gerstner waves, foam, refraction, etc.   
  
And water is probably currently the easiest thing to get the current models to do when it comes to natural phenomena, there's dozens if not hundreds of videos from people literally getting really good water effects with one prompt with three.js etc. But of course when the interaction with other elements come to play it gets more complex.

replies.author: kylef5993
replies.body: Can you share the GitHub? My Claude + blender + unity pipeline can’t create water or trees in any good quality no matter how much I question it

comments.author: ChemicalScum
comments.body: Very impressive, I'm building a game that could use a world like this. How do you create the vegetation? Do you generate textures with some other model? Or is it all proc gen? How do you handle LODs? I have so many questions about things I'm struggling myself.

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body: Plants are mostly procedural, there's a few (pre-built) meshes. But they are all offline prepared, and then the presentation is more optimized so that there's preset LOD sequence, shaders, textures in runtime size, etc. Almost all of the textures are generated and then further processed to varitety of maps by the tree builder    I've set up. There's no GameObjects, almost everything is drawn as instanced geometry.
